title: Tunable target allocator with safety fences for Dedicated autoscaling
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Dedicated customers require deterministic throughput guarantees while still allowing autoscaling to reduce cost. Current autoscalers either (a) chase latency percentiles and oscillate under bursty workloads, or (b) rely on coarse thresholds that over-provision. We need a general-purpose autoscaling policy engine for Dedicated fleets that exposes tunable target metrics, multiple scaling algorithms, and explicit safety fences (surge budgets, cooldowns, and hard caps) so product and SRE can encode contracts like 99th-percentile latency windows and per-tenant committed throughput without risking runaway scale or SLA violations.

Goals:
- Expose target metrics: committed_throughput (units/sec), p95/p99 latency, queue_depth, gpu_utilization, token_rate, and a composite percentile-weighted target.
- Implement multiple scaling primitives: PID-like proportional-integral with anti-windup, multiplicative stepper for fast burst capture, and conservative additive reconcilers for cooling down.
- Provide safety fences: min_replicas, max_replicas, surge_budget (temporary headroom), cooldown_periods, grace_margin (percent above target), and cost_cap per customer/fleet.
- Rollout in a controlled manner: policy simulator, canary on test fleets, and gradual opt-in for customers.

Scope:
- Autoscaling policy language (new JSON/YAML schema) + validation API.
- Runtime controller implementing metric ingestion, estimator, and actuator with an abstraction layer so Dedicated autoscaler can be swapped between strategies at runtime.
- Observability: per-policy event stream, decision trace, and cost/latency impact dashboard entries in Console.

Non-goals:
- Replacing the existing SLA contract UI (handled by Console/PM). Not handling tenant billing changes in this ticket (billing integration to follow).
acceptance_criteria: 1) New policy schema validated by CI (+ unit tests), 2) Simulator reproduces 3 workload shapes (steady, periodic burst, heavy-tailed burst) and outputs expected scale decisions for each algorithm, 3) Controller respects surge_budget and never exceeds max_replicas in simulation or canary, 4) Decision traces are emitted to Console (events contain reason, metric snapshot, proposed action, final action), 5) Canary on 2 non-production Dedicated fleets shows p99 latency within target with no oscillation for 72h, 6) Docs and runbook written and reviewed by SRE and PM.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: metric-collector -> estimator -> policy-evaluator -> actuator.
- Metric-collector: scrape from existing telemetry (prometheus exporters / agent), normalize to a common window (30s/1m), compute percentile estimates using existing histograms.
- Estimator: maintain short-term demand forecast (EWMA + simple AR model) used by PID integrator to avoid windup on transient spikes.
- Policy-evaluator: pluggable strategy interface with three implementations: pidStrategy, multiplicativeBurstStrategy, conservativeHoldStrategy. Each strategy returns a desired_replica_delta and a confidence score.
- Safety fence enforcer: linearized checks applied after strategy output; enforcer will cap delta according to surge_budget, respect cooldown timestamps, and decrement confidence if cost_cap would be violated.
- Actuator: reconcile loop that submits scale intent to fleet-orchestrator with idempotency token and records decision trace to event-log.

Config schema highlights (examples in spec doc):
- target_metrics: [{name: "p99_latency_ms", target: 250, window: "60s", weight: 0.7}, {name: "committed_tps", target: 1200, window: "60s", weight: 0.3}]
- strategy: {type: "pid", params: {kp:0.5, ki:0.02, kd:0.0, anti_windup_window:300}}
- safety: {min_replicas:2, max_replicas:50, surge_budget:4, cooldown_secs:300, grace_margin_pct:10, cost_cap_usd_per_hour:50}

Compatibility/migration: provide a compatibility shim that maps old threshold rules to the new policy (best-effort).
rollout_plan:
1) Merge policy schema + simulator tests to feature branch, 2) Run simulator across historical traces (production anonymized) and iterate params, 3) Deploy controller in read-only mode (decision tracing only) to a single staging Dedicated fleet for 48h, 4) Canary: enable actuator for staging fleet A (non-customer), monitor 72h, rollback triggers: >10% violation of p99 target or scale oscillation detected, 5) Beta opt-in for 3 low-risk customers with explicit manual overrides, 6) Full rollout thereafter with feature flag and staged ramping.

Rollback plan: immediate disable actuator via feature flag and revert to legacy autoscaler.

Runbook: include steps to examine decision traces, force scale, and revoke surge_budget per-tenant.
test_plan:
Unit tests for schema validation and strategy math, integration tests exercising estimator with synthetic traces, simulator test-suite with seed traces (steady, wave, heavy_tail), e2e canary smoke: enable on staging fleet and assert no >5% latency regressions, chaos test: kill 30% of replicas mid-burst and verify safe re-reconciliation. Load-test: synthetic tenants with per-tenant committed throughput to validate fair-share logic.

Monitoring: SLI - p99 latency, SLO - 99% of minutes under target, alert - repeated oscillation (scale up then down >3x in 15m), cost anomaly if cost_cap breached.
notes:
Design review scheduled 2026-03-08 with SRE and PM. Recommend security review because actuator writes to fleet orchestrator. Consider KMS use for actuator idempotency tokens.

Open questions:
- How to prioritize multi-tenant contention when two tenants' surge_budgets overlap? Proposed: FIFO headroom allocator with tenant_priority override.
- Should surge_budget be billable? Deferred to PM.
- Exact mapping from percentiles to replica counts (we provide paramized mapping functions in strategy library).
